correctness.rationale: Starting with all links eligible, let b_i=A_i sgn_+(x_i) and Z=sum b_i for the next step. The mean increment is (n−1)Z/n² and the new deviation is Z/n²−b_i/n, bounded in absolute value by 2s/n. Successive confidence tests are bounded by 2s initially, 7s/2 at the second update, and 2s+4s/n thereafter using the one-step lag of expressions. Thus induction supplies complete listening under the stated inclusive threshold. At each positive time each coordinate has conditionally a non-atomic contribution from at least one other agent. While there are mixed signs, the mean lies in [−2s/n,2s/n]. Prescribing a draw in the top 1/(4n) fraction of the range for each positive sign, and in the bottom fraction for each negative sign, forces Z≥3s/4 while signs remain mixed. Prescribe by the observed signs even if absorption has already occurred, to obtain block probability exactly (4n)^(−12n) by conditional multiplication. Twelve mixed steps would increase the mean by at least 9s(n−1)/n²>4s/n, a contradiction. Uniform block minorization gives the claimed tail from time 1. Strict unanimity is absorbing, and the unconditional strong law for the iid amplitude sums applies after discarding the finite random prefix; bounded deviations transfer the signed speed to every coordinate. With constant amplitudes the ordered update values for old positive and old negative agents differ by 2s/n, so mixing requires every sign to reverse. Requiring two mixed steps intersects the intervals (−s(H+1)/n,−s(H−1)/n) and (s(H−n)/n²,s(H+n)/n²). Their overlap forces |H|<2n/(n+1), gives the three stated windows, and restores the initial mean and sign pattern after two updates. A third update repeats the first state, proving period two after at most one transient. Opposite strict signs on the first two phases give actual period two, including the n=2 case. The exhibited initial states lie strictly inside the confidence premise.
residual_risks: The paper's Table 1 specifies an amplitude between zero and s, but does not itself establish independent uniform draws; the exact law used here is the frozen theorem's explicit specialization. Equation (5) does verify the nonnegative branch at zero and Table 1 verifies no clipping.
Boundary states with zero updated coordinates are excluded from the deterministic interval classification; the stochastic null-set proof is not asserted for constant amplitudes.
